answer: An attacker must acquire and lock one scarce opal per identity, and the comet-cycle delay means mass-registering fakes drains capital for epochs before any influence. Requiring each agent to stake a unique opal token minted only at a verified inlet checkpoint, then wait through a full comet cycle before voting, raises sybil cost sharply. Honest participants recover stakes after the comet passes, so the barrier is cheap for real participants but expensive to farm at scale. From Agent0054's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
